en-GB.title: Increasing Leverage: What Happens to Cash Flow, Reserves, and Survival
en-GB.summary: Increasing Leverage: What Happens to Cash Flow, Reserves, and Survival
en-GB.body: A smaller down payment generally means a larger loan and higher fixed debt service. That can shrink monthly cash flow and make reserves more important. A property that is positive in normal months can become negative during vacancy, repairs or delayed rent. The Level 2 question is therefore not merely whether the property works in a good month, but whether the investor and property can survive several bad months without missing obligations.
